plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DESeq2 analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is an interaction question in a 2x2 factorial design (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 16 samples total, raw salmon gene counts, 12000 genes, human brain tissue). The plan follows the DESeq2 interaction-model procedure returned by the knowledge service (snapshot sha256:709bb1f7...5439): (1) QC on sample structure via blind VST/PCA/distance heatmap to confirm the four groups separate and no sample is mislabeled or an outlier before any modeling; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >= the smallest group size of 4 samples), leaving independent filtering to do the rest; (3) DESeq2's built-in median-of-ratios normalization, not a pre-normalized input; (4) an explicit factorial design genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with WT and vehicle set as reference levels; (5) DESeq2 Wald test on the interaction coefficient (does the drug's effect differ between genotypes) plus the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, and within KO) so the interaction is interpreted alongside what it modifies; (6) ashr shrinkage of each contrast (the simple-effect and interaction contrasts are not single model coefficients, so ashr rather than apeglm); (7) BH-adjusted p-values per contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering kept on and a p-value histogram diagnostic; (8) fgsea preranked GSEA per contrast against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally, human, 50 sets) using the Wald statistic as the ranking metric, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways as second/third collections (also staged locally for human) — because with n=4/cell the interaction term is likely to yield few or no significant single genes (rule R-0103/R-0039 note reduced power for interaction terms at low replicate counts), the ranked test is the primary read-out rather than an over-representation analysis of a short list; (9) a consolidated report presenting the interaction contrast and both simple effects side by side, MA/dispersion diagnostic plots, and a full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene set collection versions, random seeds). Twelve replicates in the design (16 samples total) sit at the lower edge of adequate replication for a 2x2 interaction test, so the report explicitly states the resulting power limitation rather than overclaiming a null or weak interaction result.

Simple effects + interaction contrast side by side, MA/dispersion plots, reproducibility record
